module_title: Advanced Analysis - Ecological Importance and Artificial Reservoirs
introduction: This advanced level focuses on lakes with unique ecological significance (like floating national parks), high-altitude lakes, and the largest man-made reservoirs created by damming rivers.

core_concepts.title: Loktak Lake (Manipur)
core_concepts.description: The largest freshwater lake in Northeast India. It is famous for its 'Phumdis' (heterogeneous mass of vegetation, soil, and organic matter at various stages of decomposition floating over it).

core_concepts.title: Keibul Lamjao National Park
core_concepts.description: Located on Loktak Lake, it is the only 'floating national park' in the world and the last natural refuge of the endangered 'Sangai' (dancing deer) of Manipur.

core_concepts.title: Highest Lakes
core_concepts.description: 'Cholamu Lake' (or Tso Lhamo) in Sikkim is the highest lake in India (approx 5,330m), situated near the Donkia Pass. It is the source of the Teesta River.

core_concepts.title: Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar
core_concepts.description: It is the largest 'Artificial (man-made) Lake' in India. It is the reservoir of the Rihand Dam (on the Rihand river, a tributary of the Son) located on the border of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.

core_concepts.title: Dhebar Lake (Jaisamand Lake)
core_concepts.description: Located in Udaipur, Rajasthan, it is India's second-largest artificial lake, built in the 17th century by Rana Jai Singh across the Gomati River.

important_entities.name: Chilika & Keoladeo
important_entities.significance: Chilika Lake (along with Keoladeo National Park in Rajasthan) was the first Indian wetland of international importance to be designated under the Ramsar Convention in 1981.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Govind Sagar vs. Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Do not confuse the two! 'Govind Sagar' is the reservoir of the Bhakra Dam in Himachal Pradesh (Sutlej river). 'Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar' is the reservoir of the Rihand Dam in UP/MP.

Often asked in trivia/advanced geo: Roopkund in Uttarakhand is a high-altitude glacial lake famous as the 'Skeleton Lake' because hundreds of ancient human skeletons are visible at its bottom when the snow melts.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Loktak lake is exclusively located in Manipur.

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC heavily targets Loktak Lake and the Sangai deer. Remember the term 'Phumdi'.
In Assertion-Reasoning questions, understand that artificial lakes are primarily created for hydroelectricity, irrigation, and flood control (e.g., Rihand, Bhakra).
